Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.videoplayer

Class VideoBackend

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.videoplayer.VideoBackend
public final class VideoBackend extends Object
The AWT-free video playback seam. Unlike audio, the JDK has no video decoder at all, and the project deliberately ships no third-party codec, so every video is handed to a real external player the backend resolves and drives. This mirrors the honest split the rest of the desktop uses (the Media Writer drives dd/xorriso, the Audio Player hands MP3 and streams to mpv/vlc, Video Conference hands the session to the browser): a small pure layer decides how to launch a player and builds the exact command line, while the panel performs the thin, guarded process start.

Every method here is pure and side-effect free - no process is started, no display is touched - so the whole launch-decision table is unit-testable headless. The process launch lives in VideoPlayerPanel, guarded like the desktop's other external-command paths.

    • KNOWN_PLAYERS

      public static final List<String> KNOWN_PLAYERS
      External players this backend knows how to drive, in preference order. vlc and mpv lead because they handle the widest range of containers, codecs, streams and discs out of the box.

    • playCommand

      public static List<String> playCommand(String player, String location)
      Builds the command line that plays location with player. An unknown player is invoked with just the location.
      Parameters:
      player - the executable name (e.g. vlc)
      location - the file path, stream URL or disc URL
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when either input is blank

    • playCommand

      public static List<String> playCommand(String player, String location, boolean fullscreen, int volumePercent)
      Builds the play command with optional full-screen and master volume. The volume is applied only for players that take a percentage flag (mpv, ffplay, mplayer); full-screen is applied for the players that understand a flag for it (vlc, mpv, mplayer, ffplay).
      Parameters:
      player - the executable name (e.g. vlc)
      location - the file path, stream URL or disc URL
      fullscreen - true to start in full-screen where supported
      volumePercent - the master volume 0..100, or a value outside that range to leave the player's default untouched
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when either input is blank

    • resolvePlayer

      public static Optional<String> resolvePlayer(String preferred, Predicate<String> available)
      Resolves the player to use: the preferred one when it is set and available, otherwise the first available known player.
      Parameters:
      preferred - a user-chosen player (may be null/blank for auto)
      available - a probe for whether an executable is on the PATH
      Returns:
      the player to drive, or empty when none is available
